rubriker.title: U.S. Championship: Round 10
rubriker._rss_content: Wesley So drew Hans Niemann in under an hour and leads on 7/10, a full point clear of Fabiano Caruana and Grigoriy Oparin. In the women's, rookie Rachael Li beat Rose Atwell and leads Alice Lee by a point, but Lee won too and stays alive.

Vahap Sanal and Team Türkiye triumph at NATO Chess Championship
rubriker._rss_content: Vahap Şanal won the 2026 NATO Chess Championship in Jūrmala with a perfect 7/7 score, while Türkiye took first place in the team competition. Slovenia's Laura Unuk finished second overall and was the event's top woman, with Germany's Robert Stein claiming bronze on tiebreaks. The championship brought together 148 military players from 18 NATO countries and also featured a blitz event won by Dutch IM Mark Timmermans. | Photos: Official website

rubriker.title: FIDE President Timur Turlov meets Cyprus President Nikos Christodoulides in Nicosia
rubriker._rss_content: FIDE President Timur Turlov met Cypriot President Nikos Christodoulides in Nicosia to discuss the country's growing chess infrastructure and future cooperation with FIDE. Cyprus has hosted several major international events in recent years while also expanding domestic tournaments, youth training and permanent facilities. The meeting highlighted the island's development as an emerging European chess centre and its potential as a model for combining elite events with long-term national growth. | Photo: FIDE

rubriker.title: European Club Cup - Live!
rubriker._rss_content: The European Club Cup is taking place on 17-23 October in Budva, Montenegro, bringing together 108 teams in the open section and 22 teams in the women's competition. The seven-round event features a number of elite players, including Nodirbek Abdusattorov, Wei Yi, Alexandra Goryachkina and Humpy Koneru. | Follow the action live with expert commentary starting at 14.00 CEST (8.00 ET, 17.30 IST) | Pictured: Vasyl Ivanchuk | Photo: Gerd Densing

rubriker.title: Rosenstein Keeps His CAS Appeal Over Turlov's FIDE Eligibility Alive
rubriker._rss_content: Wadim Rosenstein lost the FIDE presidential election to Timur Turlov in the second round on September 26, 110 votes to 85, but his appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport over Turlov's eligibility has not gone away.

rubriker.title: Asset-Seizure Against Turlov Withdrawn
rubriker._rss_content: Russia's Prosecutor General's Office has dropped a lawsuit seeking to seize the Russian assets of new FIDE President Timur Turlov and companies linked to his Freedom Holding group.

rubriker.title: US Championship: Round 9
rubriker._rss_content: Round 9 in Saint Louis left both sections with a clear leader and two rounds to play. In the open, Wesley So drew defending champion Fabiano Caruana in a sharp Italian and stays a full point ahead on 6.5/9, in a round with five draws and one decisive game. In the women's, rookie Rachael Li beat Nazi Paikidze after a late blunder to reach 7/9 and secure her first IM norm, while all six games were decisive.

rubriker.title: Total Chess pone sobre la mesa un sistema unificado de ratings Elo
rubriker._rss_content: Total Chess ha propuesto un nuevo sistema de puntuación que combina los ratings de los jugadores en ajedrez clásico, rápido y blitz en una sola cifra. Desarrollada por el investigador Mehmet Mars Seven en colaboración con Norway Chess, la fórmula utiliza las puntuaciones Elo existentes de la FIDE para evaluar la fuerza de juego global de los ajedrecistas en las tres modalidades. Magnus Carlsen (en la imagen) encabeza la clasificación inaugural, seguido de Hikaru Nakamura y Nodirbek Abdusattorov. El sistema será sometido a una consulta pública antes de introducir posibles modificaciones. | Foto: Nils Rohde / ChessBase
